english.title: Distort / alter evidence given / document produced / thing provided for an investigation
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) did an act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..),

(A)_[with the intention that it should]_
(B)_[knowing or believing that it was likely to]_

have the effect of distorting or otherwise altering evidence, a document or thing that is given, produced or provided for the purposes of an investigation under Part 1 of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 7(1)(a) and (6) of Schedule 6 to the Coroners and Justice Act 2009.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Paragraph 7(5) of Schedule 6 to the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 provides that proceedings for this offence may be instituted only by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
(ii) Paragraph 7(4) of Schedule 6 to the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 provides that a person does not commit an offence under paragraph 7(1) or 7(2) by doing anything that is authorised or required by a senior coroner or the Coroner for Treasure or by virtue of paragraph 2 of Schedule 5 or any privilege that applies.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 51 weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale.

In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 a reference in this Schedule to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months, paragraph 10 of Schedule 6 to the Coroners and Justice Act 2009.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
